question: Does Fowler's 1918 Philippine fish list provide a species record, collection context, or evidence for an introduction date relevant to the later Monopterus claims?

primaryArticlePage.title: A List of Philippine Fishes
primaryArticlePage.author: Henry W. Fowler
primaryArticlePage.accessStatus: JSTOR labels the item FREE and says it is openly available as part of an Open JSTOR Collection.
primaryArticlePage.copyrightNote: JSTOR states that, to its knowledge, the journal issue is in the public domain and may be used accordingly, while disclaiming representation or warranty. No independent legal determination was made.

archiveAccessChecks.observation: The catalog lists a Full view copy of Copeia no. 39–64 (1917–1918) from the University of California, which includes issue 58.

archiveAccessChecks.retrievalResult: The research web retrieval tool returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. This is an environment-specific retrieval result, not evidence that the item is universally inaccessible. No page content was retrieved.
A direct request timed out after 20 seconds in this environment. No PDF content was retrieved.

archiveAccessChecks.observation: The archive listing identifies JSTOR and HathiTrust issues from 1913–1930 as freely readable online; it is an access lead, not article-content evidence.

retrievalAssessment.whatWasReviewed: The JSTOR article landing-page metadata and terms note, the HathiTrust catalog viewability listing, and The Online Books Page archive listing were readable.
retrievalAssessment.whatWasNotReviewed: The four original article pages, including page 62, were not retrieved or visually read. HathiTrust's catalog lists a full-view issue, but the linked item returned HTTP 403 to this research retrieval tool; the direct JSTOR PDF request timed out. These results do not establish general user inaccessibility. No direct Fowler wording or original specimen label has been verified; Herre's separate 1923 OCR-only summary is documented in ncr-monopterus-herre-1923-source-context-review-20261120. No collection date, catalog number, accession number, or exact Fowler locality is confirmed.
retrievalAssessment.secondaryCrossReference: FishBase's Monopterus albus reference list maps Fowler 1918 to the historical name Fluta alba on page 62. Herre's 1923 page-125 scan OCR also reports that Fowler's specimen was labeled only Philippine Islands; see ncr-monopterus-herre-1923-source-context-review-20261120. This is provisional OCR from a later secondary account and does not substitute for reading Fowler's primary page or inspecting the original specimen label.
retrievalAssessment.bibliographyCrossReference: The NFRDI-hosted bibliography of Philippine fishes independently lists the same Fowler citation and pages 62–65.

evidenceLimits.dateInterpretation: A 1918 publication or list entry does not establish when any fish was introduced, first arrived, or was collected.
evidenceLimits.taxonomicIdentity: The historical name Fluta alba and later Monopterus albus usage do not by themselves identify the modern taxon of the referenced specimen or population.
evidenceLimits.localityAndSpecimens: Herre's 1923 OCR-only account reports a general Philippine Islands label, but no Pasig or NCR locality, waterbody, collection date, catalog number, accession number, or specimen determination is verified.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain Fowler as a primary-page review lead. Public archive routes were identified, but the article pages were not retrieved in this environment; do not present this as a completed primary-source review. Herre's later OCR-only account supplies broad Philippine Islands label context but no waterbody, collection date, or identifier. Keep the 1918 publication year separate from any introduction-year claim.

nextActions: If a permitted retrieval path becomes available, review page 62 plus any surrounding note; record only Fowler's verbatim historical name and directly stated source context. Do not bypass a 403, login, or other access control.
Keep Herre's provisional 1923 account as separate historical context; do not attribute it as a verified reading of Fowler or equate its specimen with the later Smithsonian lots.
Seek the catalog/accession identifiers behind the reported 14-lot reclassification; do not infer Fowler's specimens are among those lots without a matching identifier.
